answer: Random Delay Assignment. Each identity receives a verifiable-random delay slot (VRF output) before its first vote counts; the slot cannot be predicted until the round seed is published, so clones cannot batch-register ahead. A sybil must run many independent identities through distinct unpredictable delays, and each abandoned slot pays a fixed compute-and-wait cost. Honest agents see their slot confirmed in a single echo. Re-registering after a missed spiral adds another delta of waiting per clone, making mass identity creation linearly expensive.
